problem_text:
A logistics manager needs to distribute a total shipment volume across 11 distribution centers to maximize overall delivery efficiency.  
The characteristics of each center are as follows:  
* Center A: delivery efficiency 0.080, handling difficulty 0.071, capacity limits [0.035, 0.457]  
* Center B: delivery efficiency 0.034, handling difficulty 0.211, capacity limits [0.038, 0.363]  
* Center C: delivery efficiency 0.082, handling difficulty 0.112, capacity limits [0.083, 0.505]  
* Center D: delivery efficiency 0.078, handling difficulty 0.238, capacity limits [0.079, 0.833]  
* Center E: delivery efficiency 0.135, handling difficulty 0.219, capacity limits [0.058, 0.397]  
* Center F: delivery efficiency 0.193, handling difficulty 0.024, capacity limits [0.076, 0.345]  
* Center G: delivery efficiency 0.168, handling difficulty 0.137, capacity limits [0.023, 0.865]  
* Center H: delivery efficiency 0.141, handling difficulty 0.132, capacity limits [0.045, 0.887]  
* Center I: delivery efficiency 0.151, handling difficulty 0.058, capacity limits [0.080, 0.503]  
* Center J: delivery efficiency 0.080, handling difficulty 0.130, capacity limits [0.003, 0.891]  
* Center K: delivery efficiency 0.022, handling difficulty 0.266, capacity limits [0.002, 0.836]  

Each center must be allocated a fraction of the total shipment volume within its specified capacity range, and all allocations must sum to one.  
To ensure operational readiness, the manager requires that the group of high-priority centers, represented by the set L = {A, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K}, collectively receive at least 0.401 of the total volume.  
Additionally, the overall handling difficulty of the distribution plan must not exceed 0.150, and the total delivery efficiency must be at least 0.064.  
Determine the optimal shipment allocation that maximizes total delivery efficiency while satisfying all constraints.
